name: AutoGPT
tagline: Autonomous general-purpose AI agent coordinating goal decomposition and plugin tools.
risk_reasons: Continuous mode (--continuous) disables all human approval gates, allowing autonomous destructive action chains.
Plugin architecture allows third-party extension code execution without cryptographic signatures.
Recursive tool calls can exhaust upstream LLM budget in short intervals.
ai_report:
AutoGPT remains one of the most prominent open-source autonomous agent architectures, capable of breaking down high-level user objectives into recursive sub-tasks. The system supports web browsing, filesystem storage, and shell commands. In standard interactive mode, AutoGPT pauses before every tool execution to request operator authorization.

However, the platform includes a continuous execution switch (--continuous / -c) designed for hands-free automation. In continuous mode, all approval gates are suppressed, presenting critical operational danger if the agent encounters conflicting objectives or prompt injection payloads. In 2024, CVE-2024-38520 demonstrated that untrusted plugin manifests could execute arbitrary shell commands during discovery.

OpenSSF Scorecard evaluation scores 7.6/10. While dependency auditing and release frequency are robust, operators must treat continuous mode with extreme caution and never run AutoGPT with write access to production directories. With our 55% Security Health weighting, AutoGPT earns a Caution rating with a 79/100 Safety Score.

permission_model.approval_prompt_detail: Prompts before every tool execution in interactive mode. Suppressed entirely if launched in '--continuous' mode.
permission_model.verdict: Caution: Safe in interactive mode; high danger in continuous mode. Operators must never deploy continuous mode on sensitive host environments.

cves.summary: Arbitrary code execution via untrusted plugin manifest parser during extension discovery.

incident_history.title: AutoGPT Unverified Plugin Code Execution
incident_history.description: Third-party community plugins could execute arbitrary Python code upon import before user authorization.
incident_history.mitigation: Upgraded in v0.5.2 with strict plugin verification and isolated execution boundaries.

use_cases: General-purpose autonomous task automation and market research synthesis.
Multi-step web crawling, summarization, and data extraction pipelines.
Experimental goal decomposition and recursive agent benchmarking.

perfectFor: AI researchers and developers exploring autonomous multi-step reasoning architectures.
Power users willing to supervise execution loops in interactive mode.
skipIf: Unsupervised automated deployments on machines holding sensitive financial or corporate credentials.
Users expecting zero prompt engineering or instant guaranteed task convergence.
